bodyMd:
## What this sample is

This file is a sample used only to test the blog publisher. It is not a real article and it is never published.

The publisher refuses any slug that starts with the word sample, so a real run on this file stops before anything is sent.

A dry run reads the live post count, checks every rule on this file, confirms that each link below answers on the live site, and then stops.

Every rule the site enforces on a post is exercised by this file: the title length, the description length, the slug shape, the word count, the section count, the tag count, the question and answer pairs, and the hero image.

## What the checks cover

The title must be sixty characters or fewer, because the site adds its own name after it in the page title.

The description must be one hundred and sixty characters or fewer, because search results cut it off after that.

The slug must be lowercase words joined by single hyphens and must not already belong to a published post.

The body must run to at least nine hundred words and carry at least three second level headings, so the table of contents appears on the page.

Two to four tags are required, and three to five question and answer pairs, which the site turns into an accordion and into structured data.

The hero image must be a path from the shared library or a secure web address that the site can copy.

No text field may carry a long dash of either kind, and no text field may carry a hand typed price.

## How the cap works

The cap is three posts in any seven days. It counts every published post on the site, whoever wrote it, and a post dated in the future counts too.

The count is read before anything is written. When the cap is reached the run stops with the time the next slot opens.

Nothing in a queue file, a flag or an environment variable can raise the cap. Only a change to the script, reviewed by the owner, can do that.

Readers gain because the site cannot fill with thin pages, and the owner gains because the limit is enforced where the post is published.

## Filler for the word count

The queue branch is one of the things this sample file exists to exercise. When it is wrong the publisher names the queue branch in its list of problems and exits without writing anything to the site, which keeps the live site safe while the owner reads the message and decides what to change. Item number 1 of 16 in this list is only filler for the word count and carries no meaning of its own.
